inputBoundaryInventory.summary: The audit target is the aiohttp framework itself, so the untrusted-input boundaries are the wire-to-request pipeline and the static-file routing pipeline it implements: (1) the HTTP wire - http_parser.py:556 request-line split (method, path, version = line.split(' ', maxsplit=2)) feeding URL.build, and the feed_data/data_received protocol entry points (http_parser.py:286/:648/:785/:935, web_protocol.py:358); (2) the request object - request.path/raw_path/path_qs/rel_url.url (web_request.py:444-467 reify properties), request.rel_url.raw_path reads in the router (web_urldispatcher.py:616 StaticResource.resolve, :997 UrlDispatcher.resolve) and in normalize_path_middleware (web_middlewares.py:86-109 request.raw_path/request.path), request.headers.get reads (web_fileresponse.py:145 ACCEPT_ENCODING, web_app.py:380 EXPECT, web_urldispatcher.py:309/:804, web_protocol.py:682, web_log.py:128), request.query/query_string/cookies accessors (no read sites in the package besides their definitions); (3) routed path variables - StaticResource.resolve percent-decodes the raw path remainder into match_info['filename'] (web_urldispatcher.py:625 _unquote_path(path[len(self._prefix)+1:])), consumed in StaticResource._handle via request.match_info['filename'] (web_urldispatcher.py:635) and passed to Path() at :637 - THE dominant attacker-controlled file-location input; DynamicResource._match also percent-decodes match values (web_urldispatcher.py:472); (4) multipart upload filenames - request.post() parses multipart/form-data: field.filename from Content-Disposition (multipart.py:535-541 content_disposition_filename, web_request.py:724/:745) is stored in FileField (web_request.py:74-79) but the file content goes to an auto-named tempfile.TemporaryFile() (web_request.py:726) - the upload filename never reaches a filesystem path construction in this tree; (5) CLI - the `python -m aiohttp.web` argparse entry (web.py:599 main(sys.argv[1:]), -U/--path unix socket path arg) and tools/check_changes.py:35 Path(argv[0]); (6) environment - os.environ reads (helpers.py:197 NETRC -> Path(netrc_env) -> netrc.netrc read at :218, helpers.py:77 AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS, web_fileresponse.py:38 AIOHTTP_NOSENDFILE) - operator/local-process trust level; (7) operator-configured file paths (NOT attacker input, emitted for labeling to classify): StaticResource directory / add_static path (web_urldispatcher.py:534, :1138), CookieJar.save/load file_path (cookiejar.py:105-113, includes pickle.load), UnixSite path (web_runner.py:134). The dominant filesystem-operation channels are: pathlib stat (web_fileresponse.py:136/:141, web_urldispatcher.py:538/:584/:657/:667, helpers.py:224), pathlib open (web_urldispatcher.py:587, cookiejar.py:107 write / :112 read, web_fileresponse.py:288 bare filepath.open reference executed via run_in_executor), loop.sendfile (web_fileresponse.py:93), iterdir directory listing (web_urldispatcher.py:683), netrc file read (helpers.py:218), tempfile creation (web_request.py:726) and unix socket creation (web_runner.py:158 create_unix_server).

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO source or sink row is expected to resolve at API level: the file-access channels flow through pathlib instance attributes on local variables (filepath/self._path/self._directory) and framework-internal values (request/field/match_info) that API graphs cannot bind to stdlib members, and pathlib/yarl/netrc are not part of the database (only the aiohttp tree is). The column is kept 'ast' for all families for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, request/match_info/tempfile/os.environ name conventions). Member-name matching (.open/.stat/.resolve/...) is receiver-name-agnostic on purpose: receiver identity cannot be proven syntactically (a .resolve() on a non-path object would be a name-collision row - none observed on these paths in this snapshot, and receiver hints like filepath/self/_directory are emitted for the labeling step).

uncoveredCases: Pathlib `/` operator constructions (home_dir / '_netrc' at helpers.py:213, folder / '_find_header.c' at tools/gen.py:170/:173) are NOT captured: BinaryExpr division is used for numeric division throughout the codebase, and no receiver-type resolution exists to distinguish Path.__truediv__; these sites are documented here instead of being extracted as noisy rows.

Bare method-reference file operations are captured only for the names open/read/seek in the file-content modules (web_fileresponse.py:66/:68/:74, :288 fobj.seek/fobj.read/filepath.open passed to loop.run_in_executor; payload.py:300/:303/:348/:356 self._value.read upload-payload reads); the socket-stream self-reference at streams.py:624 (self.read) is deliberately excluded by the module restriction, and other executor-submitted bound methods elsewhere would be missed (none observed with path-relevant semantics).

Dynamic dispatch ambiguity: .resolve()/.relative_to()/.is_file() matching is name-based; a non-pathlib receiver with the same member name would produce a false candidate row (no such collision observed on the static-file path in this snapshot; receiver hints filepath/self/_directory/netrc_path are emitted for labeling).

The C-extension request-line parser (_http_parser.pyx) is not part of the database (only .py files are extracted); the http_wire family therefore covers only the pure-Python parser at http_parser.py:556. The decoded-path boundary it feeds (yarl URL) is identical to the C path, so the router-level families (rel_url.raw_path, _unquote_path, match_info['filename']) are unaffected.

Alias imports: from pathlib import Path (web_urldispatcher.py:9, helpers.py:26) vs import pathlib (web_fileresponse.py:4, cookiejar.py:6) are both matched (Name 'Path' and Attribute 'Path' on Name 'pathlib' shapes); an aliased import (from pathlib import Path as P) would be missed - not observed.

request.headers.get() sites where the header value influences only response metadata (ACCEPT_ENCODING at web_fileresponse.py:145 toggles the .gz sibling lookup; EXPECT/HOST/Accept at web_app.py:380, web_urldispatcher.py:309/:804, web_protocol.py:682, web_log.py:128) are extracted as http_header source rows; they do not control file locations and are expected to be labeled none - kept because header reads are a genuine untrusted-input family per the extraction contract.

FileField filename propagation beyond the library: applications consuming request.post() FileField.filename decide whether it becomes a filesystem path; inside this tree it never does (web_request.py:726 tempfile). The FileField definition itself is emitted as a multipart_filename source family member via field.filename reads at :724/:745.
